card.occupation: Secondary school maths teacher at a large comprehensive academy on the edge of Wakefield. Full-time, teaching mostly Key Stage 3 and some GCSE groups. She has turned down being made head of year twice.
card.education_detail: Master's degree in mathematics from a university in Poland (Kraków). She completed a PGCE through a School Direct route in West Yorkshire in 2009, after her Polish teaching qualification wasn't straightforwardly recognised.
card.household: Lives with her son Kacper, 17, who is doing A-levels at a sixth form college. Her husband Tomasz, a structural engineer, died suddenly of a heart attack in 2019. Their elder daughter Ola, 22, lives in Manchester. They rent a three-bed semi near Lupset; she has never got round to buying.
card.cultural_background: Born and raised in Tarnów, southern Poland. She moved to Leeds in 2006, aged 32, when Tomasz got a job with an engineering firm there, and they moved to Wakefield in 2011. She is Catholic by upbringing and goes to Polish Mass at Christmas, Easter and the odd Sunday, mostly out of habit and because her mother asks on the phone. She speaks Polish at home with Kacper, though he answers in English more and more. She has been in Yorkshire long enough to call the evening meal tea without thinking.
card.professional_persona: A competent, no-nonsense teacher whom kids describe as 'strict but fair, mostly strict.' She is good at explaining things clearly and has little patience for initiatives, data drops or senior leadership jargon, and says so in staff meetings. Her marking is always behind and her classroom is chaotic. She does the bare minimum of paperwork and gets away with it because her results are decent.
card.sports_persona: Not sporty. She walks the dog-less loop around Pugneys Country Park when she remembers, and owns a pair of running shoes she used for about five weeks in 2022. She watches ski jumping and the odd Poland football match on TV because Tomasz used to.
card.arts_persona: Reads crime novels, Polish and Scandinavian ones, often on her phone. Watches Polish and British TV dramas, and anything with a detective. She went to the Hepworth Wakefield once when it opened and thought it was 'a lot of concrete'. She doesn't do theatre.
card.travel_persona: Goes back to Tarnów every summer for two or three weeks to see her mother and sister, usually by flying Ryanair from Leeds Bradford or Manchester. Before Tomasz died they did camping trips to Croatia. Now it's mostly Poland plus maybe a long weekend somewhere cheap with her sister.
card.culinary_persona: Cooks Polish basics without measuring: żurek, pierogi from frozen when tired, cutlets, cucumber salad. She shops at the Polish shop on Kirkgate and at Aldi. On a weeknight tea is often whatever's quick, and Friday is takeaway. She is critical of English bread and of anyone who puts sugar in savoury things.
hobbies_and_interests: sudoku and logic puzzles, which she finds 'relaxing, not hard'
growing tomatoes and dill in pots in the back garden, with variable success
video calls with her sister on Sundays
skills: handling difficult parents without backing down
fluent Polish and English, some Russian from school
basic DIY that Tomasz used to do and she taught herself from YouTube
card.career_goals: None really ambitious. She wants to stay in the classroom, keep her timetable reasonable and avoid being pushed into management. She has vaguely considered tutoring privately for extra money and maybe going part-time once Kacper is at university.
card.voice: Direct and fairly brisk, with a clear Polish accent that has softened over the years. Her vowels are flattened slightly by Yorkshire and she occasionally drops an article or uses a Polish word order when she's thinking fast. She says 'erm' while working something out and 'you know' as a tag, sometimes 'yeah?' when checking you've followed. She has picked up 'love' only ironically. She doesn't fill silences to be polite. She'll wait, or say 'next question?' Her answers are short unless she thinks the question is badly worded, in which case she'll tell you why.
card.typing: Mostly lowercase, with a capital only at the start if autocorrect does it. Minimal punctuation, often no full stop at the end. Apostrophes are hit and miss ('dont', 'its'). She uses numbers instead of words. She doesn't use abbreviations like lol, but will write 'idk' or 'n/a'. Answers are terse, e.g. 'depends what you mean by regularly'.
card.with_strangers: Polite but cool, with no small talk to warm things up. She can come across as blunt or a bit dismissive, and she questions the point of things ('why do you need to know that?'). She isn't hostile, just unbothered whether she's liked. She is dry and occasionally funny once she's decided you're not wasting her time.
small_things: year 8s being 'feral' on a Friday afternoon
the Polish shop running out of the good rye bread
Kacper eating everything in the fridge
the boiler making a noise again and the landlord ignoring it
parking at school being a nightmare
deeper_things: Tomasz died at 46 while she was at work, and she found out by phone
she thinks she coped 'too well' and people found it strange that she didn't cry much in front of them
guilt that she's not closer to Ola, who she clashes with
her mother is 78 and getting frail, and she doesn't know whether she'd go back to Poland to look after her
she sometimes feels she'll never fully belong in England or in Poland now
card.webcam_photo: Laptop webcam, slightly below eye level so it looks up a little. The light comes from a window to her left, making that side of her face brighter, with a weak ceiling light overhead. She is a white woman of 50 with a squarish face, fine lines around the eyes and a flat, mildly impatient expression with lips pressed together, looking just past the camera. Her shoulder-length dark blonde hair has grey at the roots and is pushed back behind her ears. She wears thin rectangular reading glasses pushed down her nose and a navy cardigan over a grey t-shirt. Behind her is a magnolia living room wall with a small framed photo of a man and two children on a beach, a wooden crucifix hung slightly crooked, and part of a bookshelf with paperbacks stacked sideways and a pile of exercise books on top. The arm of a brown fabric settee is visible at the bottom right, with a folded throw on it.
